atoms.b:
1. Slavery and the Civil War

For a long time, African Americans were held as ((slaves)) in the Southern states. In 1861, the Civil ((War)) began between the Northern and the Southern states. One big reason was slavery, which President Lincoln wanted to end. After the North won, slavery was officially ended by the 13th, 14th and 15th ((++Amendments law)).

2. Segregation and Discrimination

Even after slavery ended, African Americans were still not treated ((equally)). The 14th and 15th Amendments gave them citizenship and voting ((rights)). But new laws called ((++Jim Abraham)) Crow Laws made segregation legal. Black and white people had to use ((++separate same)) schools, buses, and toilets. This was very unfair.

3. Civil Rights Movement

In 1955, ((++Rosa Martin)) Parks refused to give up her bus seat. This marked the beginning of the Montgomery Bus ((Boycott)), which lasted over a year. One leader of the resulting Civil Rights ((Movement)) was Martin Luther King Jr. He gave his famous “I Have a ((Dream --Word))” speech in 1963. He believed in peaceful protest. In 1968, he was sadly ((murdered)).

Progress and Protests Today

In 2008, Barack ((Obama --Trump)) became the first African American ((President)) of the United States. Lately, the Black ((Lives)) Matter movement fought against ((racism)) and police violence. It became very active after the killing of George Floyd in 2020. The movement called for justice, ((equality)), and fairness for all.
